faqs.title: Frequently asked questions
faqs.intro: Common questions about retention analytics with OpenPanel.

items.question: What's the difference between retention and funnel analysis?
items.answer: Funnels answer "where do users drop off in a sequence?" Retention answers "of the users who did X, how many came back to do Y?" Both use the same events; retention focuses on repeat behavior over time, funnels on one-time flows.

items.question: Can I use any events for retention?
items.answer: Yes. You choose an initial event (e.g. signup_completed, first_purchase) and a return event (e.g. session_started, feature_used). OpenPanel cohorts users by when they did the initial event and shows what percentage did the return event in later periods.

items.question: How do I know if my retention is good?
items.answer: There is no universal benchmark; it depends on your product and how often people should come back. What matters is the trend across cohorts and where the curve flattens. Retention gives you the numbers; you decide what "good" is.

items.question: What does "On or After" mean?
items.answer: It is the default criteria. A user counts as retained in week 3 if they did the return event in week 3 or any later week. The other option, "On", counts only week 3 itself. "On or After" gives a smooth curve of stickiness; "On" shows the actual weekly habit.

items.question: Can I break retention down by a property?
items.answer: No. Retention has no breakdown. Use filters (plan is Pro) or a cohort (in cohort: Product Hunt sign-ups) to narrow the audience, and save two reports on one dashboard to compare groups.

items.question: What is the weighted average?
items.answer: The first row of the grid. It pools all cohorts per period but leaves out cells whose period has not happened yet, so a cohort from last week does not pull the week-4 average down to zero.
